tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }

    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# E2E porting brief (read fully before editing)

Context: the OpenZeppelin Stylus library moved to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust 1.91.0. The
contracts crate (`contracts/`) is migrated and compiles on the `bench` branch, which is
your base commit. Each example under `examples/` has a contract (`src/lib.rs`), an
`export-abi` binary (`src/main.rs`) and end-to-end tests (`tests/`, gated by the `e2e`
feature). The old end-to-end framework (`lib/e2e`, `lib/e2e-proc`) is being removed. Its
replacement is the `devnet` crate (`lib/devnet`), a thin layer over the SDK devnet
(`stylus-tools`, a pinned Nitro node in Docker).

Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on the `bench` commit. Read these before
editing:
- `lib/devnet/src/lib.rs` and `lib/devnet/src/assert.rs`: the helpers you will use.
- `/tmp/bench/notes/api-map.md`: the API decisions (SDK 0.10 accessors, call contexts, `Self::Error`).
- `/tmp/bench/notes/agent-brief.md`: the general rules (no global accessors, `#[public]` tags,
  commit trailer, no commented-out code, keep every scenario).

## What you own
Only the directories listed in your task: the example crates (`src/`, `tests/`, `Cargo.toml`,
`abi/` if present) and nothing else. If you need a change elsewhere (workspace `Cargo.toml`,
`lib/devnet`, `contracts/`), do not make it; list it under "requests" in your report.

## Source migration (contract code in `examples/*/src/`)
- Apply the API map: host access through `self.vm()`, `Call::new()` / `Call::new_mutating(self)`
  bound to a local before `self.vm()` is borrowed, concrete error types in `#[public]` impls
  (`Result<_, Self::Error>` fails under `export-abi`: write the concrete type), no
  `stylus_sdk::{evm,msg,block,contract}`, no `stylus_sdk::call::{Error,MethodError}`.
- Keep the ABI, selectors, error types and behaviour exactly as they are.
- `main.rs` (export-abi binary) keeps working: `cargo check -p <crate> --features export-abi`.

## End-to-end test migration (`examples/*/tests/`)
Keep the file gating `#![cfg(feature = "e2e")]` and the crate's `e2e = []` feature.

Replace the old helpers as follows:

| v0.3.0 (`e2e`)                              | new (`devnet`)                                            |
|---------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| `#[e2e::test] async fn t(alice: Account) -> Result<()>` | `#[tokio::test] async fn t() -> eyre::Result<()> { let alice = devnet::funded_account().await?; ... }` (add more accounts with `devnet::funded_account()`; each account gets 10 ETH) |
| `alice.as_deployer().with_constructor(ctr).deploy().await?.contract_address` | `devnet::deploy(&alice, devnet::wasm_path("<crate-name>"), Some((arg1, arg2, ...).abi_encode_params().into())).await?` (`use alloy::sol_types::SolValue`) |
| `alice.as_deployer().deploy().await?.contract_address` (no constructor) | `devnet::deploy(&alice, devnet::wasm_path("<crate-name>"), None).await?` |
| `constructor!(...)` / `default_ctr()` helpers | the tuple of constructor args, ABI-encoded as above (keep the helper function names if they still read well) |
| `alice.wallet` (typed contract handle)      | `Contract::new(addr, alice.provider().await?)` (the sol! bindings in `tests/abi/mod.rs` stay as they are if they compile) |
| `send!(x)`                                  | `x.send().await` |
| `watch!(x)`                                 | `x.send().await?.watch().await?` |
| `receipt!(x)`                               | `x.send().await?.get_receipt().await?` |
| `x.reverted_with(E)` on `alloy::contract::Error` | `devnet::assert::reverted_with(&err, &E { .. })` |
| `x.reverted_with(E)` on `eyre::Report` (deployment) | `devnet::assert::deployment_reverted_with(&report, &E { .. })` |
| `x.panicked_with(code)` (`Panic`)           | `devnet::assert::is_execution_revert(&err)` (the same strength as v0.3.0; do not claim a panic code you cannot see) |
| `receipt.emits(E { .. })` (`EventExt`)      | `devnet::assert::emits(&receipt, &E { .. })` |
| `ContractInitializationError` marker        | the `deployment_reverted_with` check above |

   or merge a test. If an old assertion is weaker than what the chain now reports, you may
   strengthen it; say so in the report.
2. Each test uses its own accounts (`devnet::funded_account()`), so tests can run in parallel.
3. Test names stay the same (the test inventory is compared name by name).
4. No commented-out code, no `#[ignore]` added. If v0.3.0 had an `#[ignore]` on a test, keep it
   and say why in the report.

    cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p <crate> [-p <crate> ...]

  `cargo check -p <crate> --features export-abi`, and the wasm build above.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p <crate> --all-targets --features e2e -- -D warnings` (fix warnings in your files).
- Formatting: `rustfmt +nightly-2025-08-01 --edition 2021 <your files>`.

  Do not add any other Co-Authored-By line. Do not push. Do not switch branches.

input.description: Port benches, template, and basic examples to devnet
input.prompt:
Read the E2E porting brief at /tmp/bench/notes/e2e-brief.md and follow it exactly. It also points to the API map and the general agent brief; read those too.

Your worktree: /tmp/bench/wt/e5 (branch agent/e5, based on commit ac6bde4). Run every cargo and git command with `cd /tmp/bench/wt/e5` first. Use the 1.91.0 toolchain for cargo.

You OWN these directories only: benches/ (the whole crate), templates/crypto-erc20/ (excluded from the workspace; it still uses motsu and SDK 0.9.0, so migrate it to the same SDK 0.10.10 and alloy 1.6.0 pins as the workspace, and to TestVM), examples/basic/token, examples/basic/script.

Specific requirements for benches/:
1. The benches measure gas per function, fresh and cached, for every bench group in benches/src/main.rs. Keep every group and every measured call, so the report keeps the same rows.
2. Replace the e2e framework with devnet helpers. Deployments use devnet::deploy with the WASM from a directory, not from the workspace target, so add an override: read the environment variable BENCH_WASM_DIR when it is set (the directory that holds the <name>.wasm files), and default to the workspace target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release directory otherwise. We will run the same benches on v0.3.0 WASMs and on the new WASMs against the same devnet, so the harness must not care which build it gets. Put that logic in the benches crate (not in lib/devnet, which you do not own).
3. Gas numbers come from the receipts (L2 gas used, as the old report does; keep get_l2_gas_used and the report format).
4. Keep the optimisation options (Opt::None, Opt::Cache, Opt::CacheWasmOpt): they choose which WASM file is deployed and whether the contract is cached on chain. Cache with `cargo stylus cache bid` is not available from the devnet helper; implement caching through the ArbWasmCache precompile with alloy (the sol! binding for ArbWasmCache.cacheProgram, which the SDK's stylus-tools also uses), or document in the report which options you could not reproduce.
5. The old `scripts/bench.sh` runs `cargo run -p benches`. Keep that working.
6. Do not run the benches yourself on the shared devnet while other agents run E2E tests: the lockf convention applies to benches too. Use `RPC_URL=http://localhost:55000 lockf /tmp/bench/e2e.lock cargo run -p benches` when you need a run, and write the output to /tmp/bench/logs/e5-bench.log.

Requirements for templates/crypto-erc20: it is a template crate. Its tests must keep every test name and every assertion, use TestVM, and build for wasm32 and native.

Requirements for examples/basic/token and examples/basic/script: port them like the other examples. Their scripts are plain binaries that deploy and call contracts; keep their behaviour.

Write check logs under /tmp/bench/logs/e5-*.log. Your final message is the report described in the brief (at most 40 lines), including the bench output summary (number of rows, and any group that failed).

input.description: Port benches, template, and basic examples to devnet
input.prompt:
Read the E2E porting brief at /tmp/bench/notes/e2e-brief.md and follow it exactly. It also points to the API map and the general agent brief; read those too.

Your worktree: /tmp/bench/wt/e5 (branch agent/e5, based on commit ac6bde4). Run every cargo and git command with `cd /tmp/bench/wt/e5` first. Use the 1.91.0 toolchain for cargo.

You OWN these directories only: benches/ (the whole crate), templates/crypto-erc20/ (excluded from the workspace; it still uses motsu and SDK 0.9.0, so migrate it to the same SDK 0.10.10 and alloy 1.6.0 pins as the workspace, and to TestVM), examples/basic/token, examples/basic/script.

Specific requirements for benches/:
1. The benches measure gas per function, fresh and cached, for every bench group in benches/src/main.rs. Keep every group and every measured call, so the report keeps the same rows.
2. Replace the e2e framework with devnet helpers. Deployments use devnet::deploy with the WASM from a directory, not from the workspace target, so add an override: read the environment variable BENCH_WASM_DIR when it is set (the directory that holds the <name>.wasm files), and default to the workspace target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release directory otherwise. We will run the same benches on v0.3.0 WASMs and on the new WASMs against the same devnet, so the harness must not care which build it gets. Put that logic in the benches crate (not in lib/devnet, which you do not own).
3. Gas numbers come from the receipts (L2 gas used, as the old report does; keep get_l2_gas_used and the report format).
4. Keep the optimisation options (Opt::None, Opt::Cache, Opt::CacheWasmOpt): they choose which WASM file is deployed and whether the contract is cached on chain. Cache with `cargo stylus cache bid` is not available from the devnet helper; implement caching through the ArbWasmCache precompile with alloy (the sol! binding for ArbWasmCache.cacheProgram, which the SDK's stylus-tools also uses), or document in the report which options you could not reproduce.
5. The old `scripts/bench.sh` runs `cargo run -p benches`. Keep that working.
6. Do not run the benches yourself on the shared devnet while other agents run E2E tests: the lockf convention applies to benches too. Use `RPC_URL=http://localhost:55000 lockf /tmp/bench/e2e.lock cargo run -p benches` when you need a run, and write the output to /tmp/bench/logs/e5-bench.log.

Requirements for templates/crypto-erc20: it is a template crate. Its tests must keep every test name and every assertion, use TestVM, and build for wasm32 and native.

Requirements for examples/basic/token and examples/basic/script: port them like the other examples. Their scripts are plain binaries that deploy and call contracts; keep their behaviour.

Write check logs under /tmp/bench/logs/e5-*.log. Your final message is the report described in the brief (at most 40 lines), including the bench output summary (number of rows, and any group that failed).

# Security review brief (read fully before starting)

Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust), being migrated to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
1.91.0. The `bench` branch already contains the migrated contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
clean with `-D warnings`, and all 632 unit tests pass (`cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p openzeppelin-stylus --lib`).

Your worktree is given in your task; it is based on `bench`. Run every cargo and git command in it.
Use the 1.91.0 toolchain. The checks: `cargo +1.91.0 nextest run -p <crate> --lib`,
`cargo +1.91.0 clippy -p <crate> --all-targets -- -D warnings`,
`cargo +nightly-2025-08-01 fmt -p <crate> -- --check`.

## Goals (from the project owner, verbatim intent)
1. Full security review of the code in your scope.
2. Look for what the reports in audits/ missed.
3. List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
4. Describe every finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact, and the severity.
5. For each NEW bug: commit a FAILING proof-of-concept test first, then the fix in a SEPARATE commit.
   The PoC commit must fail (show the failing output in your report); the fix commit makes it pass.
6. Do not trust audits/. Check every finding the audits mark as resolved (the audit review is
   already done; see below) and fix the ones that are only partly fixed or not fixed, when they
   are real issues in the code.
7. Do not use mutation testing or formal verification.

## Known starting points (already verified by reading the v0.3.0 code)
Full table: /tmp/bench/notes/audit-findings.md. Items that are NOT really fixed in v0.3.0, which
you must re-verify on the migrated code and fix if still real:
- v0.3.0 H-01 (PARTIAL): Baby Jubjub generator is not in the prime-order subgroup
  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/baby_jubjub.rs:15-17). Bandersnatch and Jubjub were fixed.
- v0.3.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): the UUPS version check can never tell implementations apart: it compares
  against a fixed library constant (contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:54, 434-436,
  495-504).
- v0.2.0 L-09 (PARTIAL): Uint::eq still exits early (lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:181-188).
- v0.2.0 N-01 (NOT FIXED, low): verify_multi_proof and verify_with_builder lack #[must_use]
  (lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59, 128, 181).
- v0.1.0 L-03 (PARTIAL): transfer_from spends the allowance before checking the recipient
  (contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs; matches Solidity's order, gas only).
- Observation: EdDSA signing uses variable-time scalar multiplication with secret scalars
  (lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66-96). Assess whether it is reachable in an on-chain
  contract or only off-chain, and document the answer.
- Ignored tests that describe behaviour the code does not have (investigate each: real bug, or a
  wrong test). Do not simply un-ignore a test whose expectation is unmet:
  - contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/wrapper.rs: deposit_for_reverts_when_unsupported_token
    (deposit_for never returns UnsupportedToken).
  - contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs: recover_reverts_when_invalid_underlying
    (_recover reports the wrapper's own address in ERC20InvalidUnderlying, the test expects the
    underlying token's).
  - contracts/src/proxy/beacon/upgradeable.rs (or erc1967/utils.rs): the test
    upgrade_beacon_to_and_call_with_beacon_returning_invalid_implementation (TestVM does not roll
    back storage on a failed call; check whether the library relies on rollback).
  Find every other #[ignore] in your scope (grep) and classify it the same way.

## Test-harness facts you need
- stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM: `TestVM::default()`, `T::from(&vm)`, `vm.set_sender`, `vm.set_value`,
  `vm.set_block_timestamp`, `vm.set_chain_id`, `vm.set_balance`, `vm.get_emitted_logs()`,
  `vm.mock_call(addr, data, result)`, `vm.mock_delegate_call`, `vm.mock_static_call`,
  `vm.set_code(addr, code)`. Mock return data is ONE shared buffer, so register the mock right
  before the call that needs it.
- TestVM does not record calls, and a call that matches no mock still succeeds (returns the last
  mocked data). Tests that depend on a call failing must mock the failure explicitly.
- Shared helpers: contracts/src/test_utils.rs (ALICE, BOB, CHARLIE, DAVE).
- proptest is available (dev-dependency of lib/crypto; add it to contracts dev-dependencies
  through the workspace if you need it: `proptest.workspace = true`).

## How to work
- Start with the invariants: for each contract in your scope, write the invariants down (what must
  always hold: balances sum to total supply, a role admin can grant, a proof verifies only the
  leaves it commits to, a proxy only delegates to an implementation with code, and so on). Keep
  them in your notes file.
- Then attack each invariant: read the code paths that change the state, look for missing checks,
  wrong order of effects and interactions (reentrancy through the SDK call model, the TestVM
  return-data quirk does not apply to the chain), integer rounding and overflow, signature
  malleability and replay, unchecked external return values, storage-layout assumptions, and
  access-control gaps. Use tests (TestVM and proptest) to confirm.
- For each suspected bug: (1) write a PoC test that FAILS on the current code, make a commit with
  message `test(security): PoC for <id>` containing only the test; run the test to show it fails;
  (2) write the fix in a separate commit `fix(security): <short title>`; the PoC then passes.
  Never commit a PoC that you have not seen fail.
- A finding that is not a bug (the code is correct, the test was wrong, or the behaviour is by
  design) gets a note in your report with the reasoning and evidence, and no commit.
- Keep public ABI and behaviour unless a fix requires a change; document any API change in the
  report (the upgrade guide needs it).

## Commit rules
- Message style: `test(security): ...`, `fix(security): ...`, `docs(security): ...`.
- End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- Do not push. Do not switch branches. Do not touch other worktrees.

## Output
Write your findings to the notes file named in your task, one entry per finding, with these fields:
- ID (SEC-<area>-<n>), title, severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low/Informational) and why,
- where (file:line), what breaks, how to trigger it (the PoC test name), impact,
- status: NEW (not in audits/) or EXISTING (the audit finding ID), fix commit or "no change".
Also list every invariant you wrote down, and the outcome of each attack (broken with PoC,
held with the reason, or not tested with the reason).

Final message (at most 40 lines): the counts by severity, the finding IDs with their fix commits,
the PoC names, the test counts before and after, and anything you could not finish.

`cargo stylus check` exits 1 when no `Stylus.toml` is found, and it exits 0 from a project root that has one. So the scripts will run from the repository root, and the root needs a `Stylus.toml`, the same way the SDK repository has one. I'll write the scripts for the devnet, E2E, bench, and WASM check, and add the root `Stylus.toml`.

input.command:
printf '[workspace]\n\n[workspace.networks]\n' > Stylus.toml && cat > scripts/devnet.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Starts or stops the Stylus SDK devnet (a pinned Nitro node in Docker) used by the
# end-to-end tests and the benches.
#
#   scripts/devnet.sh start   builds the devnet binary, starts a node in the background
#                             and prints its RPC URL once it is ready.
#   scripts/devnet.sh stop    stops the node that `start` launched.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
STATE="$ROOT/target/devnet"
mkdir -p "$STATE"

case "${1:-}" in
  start)
    cargo build -p devnet --bin devnet --quiet
    "$ROOT/target/debug/devnet" > "$STATE/devnet.log" 2>&1 &
    echo $! > "$STATE/devnet.pid"
    until grep -q 'RPC_URL=' "$STATE/devnet.log"; do
      if ! kill -0 "$(cat "$STATE/devnet.pid")" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "the devnet exited, see $STATE/devnet.log" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      sleep 2
    done
    grep -o 'RPC_URL=.*' "$STATE/devnet.log" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-
    ;;
  stop)
    if [ -f "$STATE/devnet.pid" ]; then
      kill -INT "$(cat "$STATE/devnet.pid")" 2>/dev/null || true
      rm -f "$STATE/devnet.pid"
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 start|stop" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
EOF
cat > scripts/e2e-tests.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Runs the end-to-end tests of the examples against a Stylus SDK devnet.
#
# One devnet serves the whole run: set RPC_URL to reuse a running node, otherwise a
# devnet is started here and stopped at the end. Extra arguments are passed to
# `cargo test`, for example `scripts/e2e-tests.sh -p erc20-example`.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

if [ -z "${RPC_URL:-}" ]; then
  RPC_URL="$(scripts/devnet.sh start)"
  export RPC_URL
  trap 'scripts/devnet.sh stop' EXIT
fi

# The tests deploy the release WASM of each example.
cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown

if [ "$#" -eq 0 ]; then
  PACKAGES=$(cargo metadata --format-version=1 --no-deps \
    | jq -r '.packages[] | select(.features | has("e2e")) | .name' \
    | sed 's/^/-p /' | tr '\n' ' ')
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  cargo test $PACKAGES --features e2e --tests
else
  cargo test --features e2e "$@"
fi
EOF
cat > scripts/bench.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Gas benchmarks. Builds the examples for wasm, optimizes them with wasm-opt, and runs
# the benches against a Stylus SDK devnet.
#
# Environment:
#   RPC_URL         a running devnet; a fresh one is started for the run when unset.
#   BENCH_WASM_DIR  directory with the <name>.wasm files to benchmark; defaults to the
#                   release output of this workspace. Point it at another build to
#                   compare two versions on the same devnet.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

if [ -z "${RPC_URL:-}" ]; then
  RPC_URL="$(scripts/devnet.sh start)"
  export RPC_URL
  trap 'scripts/devnet.sh stop' EXIT
fi

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown

WASM_DIR="${BENCH_WASM_DIR:-$ROOT/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release}"
export BENCH_WASM_DIR="$WASM_DIR"

# Optimize every example's WASM for gas usage (binaryen 116, as the gas workflow pins).
for manifest in examples/*/Cargo.toml examples/*/*/Cargo.toml; do
  [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue
  name=$(grep -m1 '^name = ' "$manifest" | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"')
  bin="${name//-/_}.wasm"
  if [ -f "$WASM_DIR/$bin" ]; then
    wasm-opt --enable-bulk-memory -O3 -o "$WASM_DIR/${bin%.wasm}_opt.wasm" "$WASM_DIR/$bin"
  fi
done

export DEPLOYER_ADDRESS=0xcEcba2F1DC234f70Dd89F2041029807F8D03A990
cargo run -p benches
EOF
cat > scripts/check-wasm.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Checks every example's release WASM against the Stylus size limit with cargo-stylus.
# Runs against RPC_URL (a devnet) when set, otherwise against the Arbitrum Sepolia RPC.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

ENDPOINT="${RPC_URL:-https://sepolia-rollup.arbitrum.io/rpc}"

cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown

FAILED=0
for manifest in examples/*/Cargo.toml examples/*/*/Cargo.toml; do
  [ -f "$manifest" ] || continue
  name=$(grep -m1 '^name = ' "$manifest" | grep -oE '"[^"]+"' | tr -d '"')
  wasm="target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/${name//-/_}.wasm"
  [ -f "$wasm" ] || continue
  echo "checking $name"
  if ! cargo stylus check -e "$ENDPOINT" --wasm-file "$wasm"; then
    FAILED=1
  fi
  sleep 2
done
exit $FAILED
EOF
git rm -q scripts/nitro-testnode.sh && chmod +x scripts/devnet.sh scripts/e2e-tests.sh scripts/bench.sh scripts/check-wasm.sh && bash -n scripts/devnet.sh && bash -n scripts/e2e-tests.sh && bash -n scripts/bench.sh && bash -n scripts/check-wasm.sh && echo "syntax ok" && ls scripts

# Documentation brief (read fully before editing)

Project: OpenZeppelin contracts for Stylus (Rust). The library moved to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on Rust
1.91.0. The code on your base commit is final for the contracts crate: it compiles, clippy is
clean, and the unit tests pass. The examples and the end-to-end tests are being ported in parallel
by other agents; do not depend on their exact text.

Your worktree is given in your task (based on the `bench` commit). Run every command in it.

## What you own
- docs/modules/ROOT/pages/*.adoc (the Antora docs pages, about 37 files), and docs/antora.yml
  and the docs navigation if it needs an update (do not change the docs build tooling).
- README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, GUIDELINES.md, CHANGELOG.md at the repository root.
- Nothing else. Do not edit contracts/, examples/, benches/, lib/, scripts/, .github/, or any
  manifest. If something there is wrong, list it in your report under "requests".

## What must be true after your work
1. Every code snippet matches the current API. Verify each snippet against the source: grep for
   the function, the type and the trait it uses. Known changes from v0.3.0 (use these exact
   forms):
   - Host access goes through `self.vm()`. There are no free functions `msg::sender()`,
     `msg::value()`, `contract::address()`, `contract::balance()`, `block::timestamp()`,
     `block::chainid()` or `evm::log(..)`. The replacements are `self.vm().msg_sender()`,
     `self.vm().msg_value()`, `self.vm().contract_address()`, `self.vm().balance(addr)`,
     `self.vm().block_timestamp()`, `self.vm().chain_id()` and `self.vm().log(Event { .. })`.
   - In a `#[public] impl Trait for Contract`, write the concrete error type
     (`type Error = Error; ... -> Result<bool, Error>`). `Result<bool, Self::Error>` does not
     compile under the `export-abi` feature.
   - Calls to other contracts take the host first and a call context second:
     `IErc20::new(addr).balance_of(self.vm(), Call::new(), who)`; a mutating call builds
     `Call::new_mutating(self)` into a local before `self.vm()` is borrowed.
   - Tests use `stylus_sdk::testing::TestVM` (the motsu framework is gone). Snippets must not show
     `#[motsu::test]`.
   - The end-to-end tests run against the Stylus SDK devnet through the `devnet` crate (see below).
   - `IEip712` methods `chain_id()` and `contract_address()` take `&self`.
   - `Erc1967Utils` and `StorageSlot` functions take `context` (or `self`) first.

   `wasm32-unknown-unknown`), and cargo-stylus 0.10.10 for deployment (`cargo install --locked
   cargo-stylus@0.10.10`). Keep the badges and the links that still work.

   Docker for the end-to-end tests), testing (nextest; TestVM for unit tests), the end-to-end
   workflow (`scripts/e2e-tests.sh`; the script starts one devnet, or reuse `RPC_URL`;
   `scripts/devnet.sh start|stop`), the benches (`scripts/bench.sh`; `BENCH_WASM_DIR` selects the
   WASM to measure), fuzzing (cargo-fuzz on nightly-2025-08-01), coverage (`cargo llvm-cov nextest`),
   the docs (`docs/` with oz-docs), and the checks (`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`).
   Remove every reference to `scripts/nitro-testnode.sh`, `lib/e2e`, `lib/e2e-proc`, `motsu`,
   `-Z build-std` and cargo-stylus 0.6.3.
4. CONTRIBUTING.md: the same prerequisites (Docker for the end-to-end tests).
5. CHANGELOG.md: add an "Unreleased" section at the top with the migration summary as Added,
   Changed, Removed. Keep it brief and factual. The full upgrade guide is written separately, so
   link to it as `docs/modules/ROOT/pages/upgrade-guide.adoc` ONLY if you create that file (you
   will not; the lead writes it), so do not link to it.
6. Every page is consistent with the others: the same names for the same things, the same
   terminology (the library is "OpenZeppelin Contracts for Stylus"), the same code style in the
   snippets (rustfmt style, 80 columns, no `msg::` calls).
7. Do not leave TODOs about things you were asked to fix. Do not comment out content.

  adoc pages): `linkspector check` (installed) or manual verification with `grep`.

  files that exist in the repository or to live URLs (the lead has network access; a 404 is a
  broken link).
- Build the docs site if the tooling is available: `cd docs && npm run docs` (this is oz-docs and
  may need network; if it fails for environmental reasons, say so and show the error).
- Code snippets that are Rust and are meant to compile: check the ones that are not marked

  workspace crate by path (`openzeppelin-stylus = { path = "<worktree>/contracts" }`, with the
  workspace's alloy and stylus-sdk versions). Report which snippets you could not compile.

## Git
- Commit in small logical commits on your branch. Message style: `docs(<area>): <what>`.
  End each commit message with only: Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- Do not push. Do not switch branches.

- Pages changed (count) and commits (`git log --oneline <base>..HEAD`).
- Snippets verified against the source and snippets compiled (counts), and the ones you left
  marked `ignore` with the reason.
